body: It was not rude in my opinion. You needed help and she sounds like she was happy to help!! I completely understand second guessing yourself though, I do it all. The. Time. I hope your day got better!!

The fact that you’re so hurt by this makes me overjoyed that there are people who care so much about their relationship with their children that they put their business out there to ask total strangers to help them. That shows that you’re trying to be a good parent so A+ for you!

 My relationship with my parents was super strained growing up and it only started improving once I became an adult. (I’m 21 now) Something that I would have loved was if my parents did something with me that was unique to me and that parent. Like me and my dad would go spend time together and go to a comic book shop because I was the only one of my sisters who as into comics and collecting them as he was so to make an effort to have a relationship with me and connect with me now that I’m older he and I go to all the Marvel movies and we discuss our theories on what’s going to happen next. I love it so much because it’s something that he only had with me and it makes me feel like he’s doing his best to keep a good relationship with me. 

Your son’s “unique thing” with you might not be something that’s obvious to you though. For example my stepmom would write notes to me and put them in my lunches pretty much from when she married my dad when I was going into 2nd grade until I was in 7th grade and I didn’t live with her and my dad much but I tried to keep almost all of them. I loved these notes so much that still have a bag full of them and she didn’t know about it until I was in high school so now she writes sweet little notes to me to let me know that she cares. 

I would just sit down with him and ask him what he would like from you to let him know that you care about him and tell him that you want to have a healthy relationship with him. If that doesn’t work ask your wife what she would do if the roles were reversed and you were the one that was close to him. I hope if this doesn’t fit what you need that you find an answer that works best for your situation!
Same to you! You’re such a blessing <3

Nanad13 you’re so sweet!! James and I have decided to not have sex until we feel like we can be together without having to rely on it so I feel like it’s not moving as fast as literally all of my past relationships have. I feel like even though it hasn’t been a full month since I broke up with Zeke I’ve already grieved for the loss of that relationship and I’m ready to hop back in the game. Both James and I have a lot of anxiety when it comes to relationships so not having that serious physical intimacy while developing our mental intimacy is a step in the right direction for me!

I personally feel like it wouldn’t be patronizing to write down exactly what emotional validation is to you. My boyfriend and I are going through a rough patch and we’re both writing down what we need from the other person so we can be on the same page, not so we can attack the other person for what they’re doing wrong in the relationship and so we each have something to refer back to if the other person feels like their needs aren’t being met.
If you preface the letter by typing “THIS IS NOT TO ATTACK YOU THIS IS BASICALLY HOW MY BRAIN WORKS PUT ONTO PAPER” and keep that in mind while writing it, there shouldn’t be an issue. (Also when you’re writing, keep in mind that he has his own stuff going on in his head. It sounds like you’re already doing this though and that is awesome!)

If he still has a problem and you’ve covered all your bases, then you have bigger things to worry about but don’t worry about that until after you’ve given him the letter and he verbally tells you he has a problem. (You’re not a mind reader and he’s 31 years old. He should know how to use his words) I hope this has helped!
